subject: Discovery recap — schema-first function-calling & deterministic JSON outputs for Acme integration
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — schema-first function-calling & deterministic JSON outputs for Acme integration

Hi Daniel — thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap from our end to make sure we captured your priorities and to propose clear next steps. Please correct me where I missed anything.

Key pain points you called out
- Downstream systems break when LLM responses are missing keys or use inconsistent types (strings vs objects).
- Human QA is costly because outputs must be normalized before downstream microservices can process them.
- Need a deterministic, auditable path for agent-driven workflows (e.g., ticket triage -> enrichment -> ticket update) so you can trace decisions back to inputs.

Current stack you described
- Node.js microservices on Kubernetes. Event bus: Kafka.
- Internal orchestration handles triage rules today; LLMs are used via a mix of OpenAI-hosted endpoints + a local Llama variant for non-critical workloads.
- Consumers expect strict JSON payloads ingested by a processing pipeline (ticket-service) with schema validation.

Success criteria you mentioned (we translated into measurable targets)
- 99% of LLM responses validate against the agreed JSON schema (primary SLO).
- < 250ms median incremental token latency for function-invocation paths in POC configuration.
- Deterministic field presence and types (no optional missing required keys for > 95% of production cases).
- Clear audit logs: decision context + model & version used + function calls invoked.

Technical notes / initial suggestions from Redwood
- We recommend a schema-first approach: provide a JSON Schema for every structured output type. Redwood runtime will prefer function-calling or structured-output modes and validate + auto-retry with guidance prompts if outputs fail schema validation.
- For agent workflows, we can map each step to a constrained function call (e.g., extract_metadata(), classify_issue(), update_ticket()) so your ticket-service receives typed payloads rather than freeform text.
- We have prefix/KV caching to reduce cost for repeated enrichment tasks and deterministic sampling controls to tighten output variance.

Attachments included
- redwood-function-calling-sample.json (small example schema + prompt templates)
- Acme-MAP-Notes.pdf (mutual action plan draft)

Proposed next steps
1) Daniel or your API team: share 1–2 representative JSON Schemas for the outputs you need (ticket-create, ticket-enrich).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with your API team + our Solutions Engineer (we suggest next week).
3) Redwood will produce a tailored POC plan (4 weeks) that includes: schema verification tests, endpoint config recommendations, and success thresholds.

Would Tuesday 2/17 or Wednesday 2/18 at 11am PT work for the technical deep dive? I linked a proposed slot below.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme-corp.com>

Cc: api-team@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — schema-first function-calling & deterministic JSON outputs for Acme integration

Thanks, Jasmine — that summary is spot on. A few clarifications and a small sample schema attached inline.

Clarifications from our side
- The critical schema is ticket-enrich (we must always include: ticket_id (string), priority (enum: low/med/high), root_cause (string), suggested_action (object with code + params)).
- Our downstream validator rejects if a required object field is null or missing; so presence matters more than ordering.
- For agent workflows: we need commas-separated audit traces (timestamped step names) stored alongside the payload. That trace must include which action invoked which function and model-version.

Acceptance criteria we will use for the POC
- Schema validation pass rate >= 99% on a 2000-sample synthetic dataset (we can share later).
- No more than 1% of responses require manual correction for shape/type errors.
- Preservation of required fields with correct types 100% of the time for high-priority tickets.

I've cc'ed our API team (api-team@acme-corp.com) — they're the ones who will share schemas and run the validation harness.

Included quick sample (inline):
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "ticket_id": { "type": "string" },
    "priority": { "type": "string", "enum": ["low","med","high"] },
    "root_cause": { "type": "string" },
    "suggested_action": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "code": { "type": "string" },
        "params": { "type": "object" }
      },
      "required": ["code"]
    },
    "audit_trace": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } }
  },
  "required": ["ticket_id","priority","suggested_action"]
}

We'll try to share the 2000-sample harness by EOD Tuesday. Tuesday works for the deep dive for most of our team; please send a calendar invite.

—Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Customer Automation | Acme Corp

Hi Daniel — looping in a couple of ops/solutions items so we capture non-functional requirements early.

Operational items we should confirm in the deep-dive
- Telemetry: you said you need token-level cost breakdowns + per-route latency percentiles. We can enable token traces and per-request model/version tags in Redwood Console.
- Data retention & security: clarify retention window for logs that include user inputs. If you need <30 days for PII-sensitive logs we can propose scrubbing or partial logging.
- Rollouts: do you need canary A/B rollout between OpenAI-hosted and Redwood-accelerated variants? We can configure fallback to the last-known-good model.

I've attached a short MAP draft (Acme-MAP-Notes.pdf) that includes these items as milestones. Also included a sample prompt pattern that increases schema-constrained outputs (see redwood-function-calling-sample.json).

For the POC we'll want: a short sandbox key, a subset of tickets (100/day) for the first 2 weeks, and access for our Solutions Engineer to a staging cluster or a mocked endpoint for validation.

Next step: Jasmine — can you send the calendar invite for Tue 2/17 at 11am PT with a Tech Deep Dive agenda (30 min tech + 30 min ops)?

Thanks — Marissa
